Anthropic’s IPO filing is shining a spotlight on the ETFs offering investors exposure to the artificial intelligence company and the infrastructure powering its growth.

The Claude maker publicly filed its S-1 registration statement with the SEC on Monday, revealing $16.3 billion in revenue for the six months ended June 2026, up sharply from $4.6 billion for the entirety of 2025. However, Anthropic also spent nearly $9 billion on AI infrastructure during the first half, exceeding its $7.3 billion expenditure for all of 2025.

The filing also highlights the scale of the company’s long-term computing needs. Anthropic has disclosed hundreds of billions of dollars in cloud and infrastructure commitments, potentially creating significant business opportunities for technology companies supplying its computing capacity.

Read Also: Potential $100 Billion Anthropic IPO Could Boost Wall Street Banks: Which ETFs Stand to Benefit?

LAZR Leads ETFs With Direct Anthropic Exposure

The Tema Photonics & Optical ETF (NYSE:LAZR) offers one of the clearest routes to pre-IPO Anthropic exposure. The fund invests in companies involved in optical networking and data movement for AI infrastructure, while holding Anthropic through a special purpose vehicle (SPV).

LAZR’s Anthropic position accounted for 10.47% of the portfolio. The SPV structure gives the fund indirect exposure to the private company rather than ownership of publicly traded Anthropic shares.

Other funds reporting Anthropic exposure include the Alger Concentrated Equity ETF (NYSE:CNEQ), Alger AI Enablers & Adopters ETF (NYSE:ALAI), KraneShares Public-Private AI & Technology ETF (NASDAQ:AGIX), Alger 35 ETF (NYSE:ATFV), Tema Electrification ETF (NASDAQ:VOLT) and iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (NYSE:BAI). Their reported Anthropic weights ranged from 1.28% for BAI to 5.28% for CNEQ.

Semiconductor ETFs Offer a Different AI Trade

Investors seeking exposure to the infrastructure behind Anthropic’s expansion can also examine the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) and iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX). Both provide exposure to chipmakers that support AI computing, although neither should be confused with a fund holding Anthropic directly.

Anthropic’s S-1 describes a multi-chip computing architecture using Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) GPUs, AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) GPUs, Amazon Web Services’ Trainium chips and Google’s tensor processing units. This diversified approach could create demand across several parts of the semiconductor and cloud ecosystem.

However, rising spending does not automatically translate into higher profits for suppliers or stronger ETF returns. Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, largely reflecting accounting charges, while its infrastructure spending and customer concentration remain important risks.

For ETF investors, the IPO presents two distinct opportunities to assess: funds offering indirect exposure to Anthropic itself and funds positioned to benefit from the infrastructure buildout. Both carry risks if AI demand, valuations or spending expectations change.

In the third quarter of 2007, insuring $10 million of Lehman Brothers’ debt for a year cost less than $100,000.

A year later, the same protection cost more than $1.4 million, and the bank had filed for bankruptcy, according to figures cited by J.P. Morgan Wealth Management.

Today, buying that insurance on CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) costs about $1.15 million a year. As a result, a comparison Wall Street had shelved for almost two decades is back.

CoreWeave’s five-year credit default swaps traded at 1,148 basis points on Monday morning, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence shared with Benzinga.

CoreWeave Default Swaps Hit Records

The spread peaked at 1,167 basis points on Oct. 22, the highest level in the 12 months of data provided by S&P Global.

One month ago, the spread stood at 835 basis points. A year ago, it was 421.

S&P Global uses a 40% recovery rate for CoreWeave. On that assumption, current pricing implies a roughly 62% chance of default over five years.

In addition, the gap with the rest of the AI trade is wide.

CoreWeave now pays about 21 times more than Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) to insure its debt. It also pays 18 times the level of the CDX North American Investment Grade Index, which stood at 63 basis points on Monday.

Five-year CDS spreads in basis points. CoreWeave as of 11:42 GMT on Oct. 26. Source: S&P Global Market Intelligence

Some Are Whispering ‘Lehman’

Bill Blain, financial strategist and CEO of Windshift Capital, drew the parallel in his Oct. 16 Morning Porridge newsletter.

“CoreWeave is way out front in the race to be the first major crash of the AI Debt Bubble. All major financial bubbles need that critical ‘wake-up-and-smell-the-money’ (or lack of it) moment. The moment when the market realises it is not in Kansas anymore,” Blain said.

“In 2007 it was the run on Northern Rock as short-term funding dried up, and later the failing Bear CDO funds… from there the crisis developed its own momentum, and soon there was the looming inevitability that a bank like Lehman was going to fail,” he added.

James Foord, an independent market commentator, went a step further in an Oct. 22 Substack post. He called CoreWeave the Lehman of this cycle, “a fair comparison given what its bonds are pricing.”

Foord then cast Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS) as this cycle’s JPMorgan, the stronger balance sheet that could survive the shakeout and pick up assets.

Read Also: Meta Just Burned Cash for the First Time Since Its IPO Year: Wall Street Raised Its Targets Anyway

J.P. Morgan Sees a Targeted Repricing

J.P. Morgan Wealth Management drew a similar parallel in an Oct. 23 note, although it did not name the company.

Global investment strategist Justin Biemann described a financing-dependent AI infrastructure borrower whose five-year CDS jumped to 1,100 basis points that week.

According to Biemann, that pricing implies a near or above 50% probability of default over five years, up from below 30% a year earlier.

“That is not a forecast, but it is difficult to dismiss,” Biemann said.

However, he stressed that the stress is targeted. Investors are demanding roughly 10 times as much to insure the weakest AI borrowers as the strongest, while broad investment-grade protection remains contained.

The concern, Biemann said, is limited to business models that need debt markets to stay open while spending stays high and cash flow stays thin.

Musk Adds to the Pressure

Meanwhile, Elon Musk added fuel on Monday.

In a post on X, he wrote that lenders have all but stopped funding companies without big revenue outside AI data centers. He also predicted “guppy-level death and consolidation” among the more than 200 neoclouds.

CoreWeave shares dropped to $51.24 early in the session, their lowest level since May 2025, before buyers stepped in. By Monday afternoon, the stock was up 3.7% at $56.24.

Even so, the stock remains 60% below its 52-week high of $141.79. Its market value of about $31 billion compares with roughly $51.6 billion of total debt, including leases.

Read Also: Nvidia Is Now Cheaper Than the Average S&P 500 Stock: Wall Street Still Sees Record Profits

Credit Is Flashing a Warning, Not a Verdict

Still, J.P. Morgan cautioned against reading CDS spreads as a countdown to default.

In 2005, the cost of insuring a major U.S. automaker’s debt surged ahead of its downgrade to junk. However, the company raised cash, restructured and never filed for bankruptcy.

Lehman followed the opposite path. Its five-year CDS climbed above 1,400 basis points by mid-September 2008, as the bank collapsed.

CoreWeave now sits about 250 basis points below that level. As a result, the cushion has grown thin, but the market is pricing a risk, not an outcome.

Which path CoreWeave takes will depend on whether lenders keep funding its buildout long enough for cash flow to catch up with its debt.

Higher gas prices for consumers since the war in Iran began are among the reasons that more voters are giving President Donald Trump poor grades in a new poll. Here’s a look at the latest favorability poll and how the economy factors in.

Trump’s Approval Hits Record Lows

Similar to recent months, approval ratings for Trump are trending lower and hitting record lows.

A new Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll for October shows Trump with a 33% approval rating, a record low for the poll. Trump’s disapproval rating stands at 66% in the poll. These figures compare to 37% and 61% in July, respectively.

The disapproval strength is also getting worse for Trump, with 52% of respondents now saying they disapprove strongly of the president.

Read Also: Where Trump’s Portfolio Meets His Power: Nvidia, Palantir, Dell and More

Economy Among Top Items

In the poll, 72% of voters say the country is headed in the wrong direction, with economic issues among the most important on the minds of voters.

Trump receives an approval rating of 28% for his handling of the economy, down from 33% in July. Back in 2018, at this point in the midterm elections, Trump’s economic approval stood at 49%.

When asked to rate the economy, 75% of voters say the economy is either not so good or poor, while 25% rate the economy excellent or good.

Ranking items on an affordability scale, gasoline is listed as being unaffordable for 71% of voters.

Groceries (60%), health care (65%) and going out to dinner (61%) also received high percentages for unaffordable on the scale.

Trump has boasted about the state of the stock market and economic health in recent months, but results from this poll point to the opposite and could lead to the Democratic Party gaining seats in Congress due to affordability being a top issue for voters in this year’s midterm elections.

SPY Stock Action

While Trump receives poor economic ratings, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY), which tracks the S&P 500, remains strong this year. The ETF is up 12% year-to-date and hit record all-time highs earlier this month.

On Monday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) warned that soaring AI investments, mounting corporate debt and insufficient regulatory oversight could expose the U.S. economy to a financial crisis reminiscent of the 2008 market crash.

Elizabeth Warren Warns of AI Bubble Risks

Warren took to X to draw parallels between today’s AI boom and the financial practices that preceded the 2008 crisis.

"Before the 2008 crash, Wall Street hid massive financial risks using accounting tricks. Now Big Tech appears to be following the same playbook," Warren wrote.

She added that Americans and the broader economy face risks because "Trump’s regulators are choosing to look the other way."

Warren shared a report titled Brace for Impact: Protecting People and the Economy When the AI Bubble Bursts, published by the Open Markets Institute and Americans for Financial Reform Education Fund.

Read Also: Elizabeth Warren Says ‘Nobody Can Seem to Explain’ What Trump’s War With Iran Accomplished as Crypto Bettors Gauge Midterm Impact

Big Tech’s AI Spending and Debt Raise Concerns

The report argues that major technology companies, including Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL), are pouring trillions of dollars into data centers and other AI infrastructure.

However, the report warns that AI-related spending is outpacing revenue from AI products and services, pushing companies to borrow more to finance their investments.

If future earnings fail to cover these costs and repay mounting debt, the resulting losses could extend beyond the technology sector.

Could An AI Crash Trigger Another Financial Crisis

The report also highlights risks from data center debt being repackaged and sold to pension funds, university endowments and other institutional investors.

Additionally, it warns that private equity firms’ investments in life insurers could expose policyholders and the broader financial system to losses.

The authors urge federal regulators, Congress and state policymakers to improve financial transparency, protect retirement savings and strengthen safeguards against systemic risks.

The report does not predict an inevitable crash. Instead, it warns that vulnerabilities are accumulating and calls for action before an AI downturn threatens wider economic stability.

news.author: Radhika Anilkumar Nadig
news.content:
China’s artificial intelligence stock selloff has erased roughly $480 billion in market value in under four months, fueling warnings that U.S. markets are showing the same signs of a bubble.

China’s AI Stocks Crash

China’s STAR50 index, which tracks its biggest AI and chip companies, has fallen about 40% after trading at nearly 250 times trailing earnings at its peak, according to Reuters and market commentator Bull Theory on X.

The country’s broad blue-chip index CSI 300 is in a bear market, down 20% from its June high, with Chinese stocks losing $3.5 trillion since their May peak.

AI stocks made up 42% of China’s market, according to the commentator, adding that “the first AI bubble has burst.”

MiniMax Group Holdings Ltd. and Zhipu AI have lost a combined $150 billion from their highs, while robot maker Unitree has fallen 50% since its August listing.

Read Also: Stock Market: Will S&P 500 Open Up or Down Today?

The US Flashes Similar Signals

AI-linked stocks account for 49% of the S&P 500’s value, according to JPMorgan, above the 42% share they held of China’s market before its crash.

The Nasdaq 100 has fallen 3.31% over the past month but remains up 16.14% year to date, while the S&P 500 is down 0.09% over the month and up 11.93% this year.

Anthropic has filed for an IPO at a valuation that could reach $2 trillion, despite losing $80.7 billion in the first half of the year. The Wall Street Journal reported it is targeting a debut the week of Nov. 16, raising $100 billion or more.

“The US is now flashing the same warning signs China did before its AI stocks crashed,” Bull Theory said.

AI Stocks Under Pressure

U.S. tech stocks have been on a rocky path this month as investors worry about the debt behind AI spending, with Meta Platforms Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) credit default swaps and CoreWeave Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:CRWV) bond yield hitting record highs.

news.author: Shomik Sen Bhattacharjee
news.content:
Noted analyst and Yorkville Ives Partner and Senior Managing Director Dan Ives dismissed concerns that Anthropic’s anticipated $1.5 trillion initial public offering could signal the peak of the artificial intelligence investment boom, despite the company’s staggering $80.7 billion first-half loss and mounting concerns over AI spending.

Ives Sees Strong Appetite Despite Massive Losses

"It’s the third inning," Ives said during a CNBC interview from Abu Dhabi, estimating that the AI revolution remains roughly 15% complete. "We’re going to go through these white-knuckle moments. This is not a top. This is not a bubble."

Anthropic’s IPO filing revealed that its first-half net loss widened to $80.7 billion, including approximately $72 billion in noncash accounting charges tied to convertible financing instruments. Revenue reached $16.3 billion, while operating losses narrowed to $693 million. Second-quarter revenue surged 1,368% year over year.

Ives expects initial investor appetite around $1.5 trillion to $1.7 trillion, below earlier expectations approaching $2 trillion. He suggested Anthropic could eventually command a $2 trillion–$3 trillion valuation, depending on its performance, but stressed that investors would scrutinize its growth trajectory and backlog.

Anthropic IPO Could Reassure AI Investors

Ives said investors should exercise caution at a $2 trillion valuation but could find a $1.5 trillion entry point attractive. "I think at two trillion, you’re not an assertive buyer," he said. However, he expects stronger demand at a lower valuation, adding, "I’d definitely be a buyer coming out."

Read Also: Anthropic’s IPO Filing Reveals Over $500 Billion AI Compute Spending Across AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, AVGO and SPCX: Top Analyst Says It Has ‘Barely Started’

His remarks reinforce his earlier prediction that Anthropic’s public debut could lift the broader technology sector.

Ives also acknowledged a "white knuckle period" for investors amid CoreWeave’s mounting debt concerns, but maintained that Anthropic remained central to the broader AI investment opportunity.

AI Safety Risks Complicate Valuation Debate

Anthropic’s prospectus outlines significant risks involving model misuse, cybersecurity vulnerabilities and potentially manipulative AI behavior. The company also faces substantial infrastructure commitments as it races to expand computing capacity.

Ives described some risks as "almost out of a sci-fi movie," adding, "The risks are real. You can’t just diminish them and kind of say that they’re not a big deal." He also questioned Anthropic’s safety-first messaging amid competition from Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) and OpenAI. "They could talk safety, but if they take their foot off the pedal," rivals would continue advancing, he argued.

Ives said the company’s push toward an IPO creates tension with CEO Dario Amodei’s calls for greater caution and guardrails around frontier AI development.

"I think for investors, it sends mixed signals," he said, arguing that Anthropic recognizes the urgency of commercialization amid intensifying competition. "It all comes down to monetization with guardrails," Ives added, emphasizing that investors must balance the industry’s enormous opportunities against the risks of increasingly powerful AI systems.

The debate follows broader concerns about AI infrastructure financing, but Ives remains convinced the industry has far more room to grow. "This is what I view as kind of just the next stage of the modernization phase of AI revolution taking place. But it is not the top in my opinion," he said.

news.author: Anusuya Lahiri
news.content:
Anthropic’s looming IPO is putting its financial strength in the spotlight, with Wall Street analysts pointing to faster-than-expected profitability, surging enterprise revenue and a massive cash cushion that could help the AI startup withstand rising compute costs and intensifying competition.

D.A. Davidson Says Profitability Is Ahead of Expectations

Anthropic could be breaking away from the AI industry’s costly spending cycle, with revenue growth far outpacing rising computing expenses.

Its roughly 1,400% first-half revenue surge, compared with a 300% increase in compute costs, coupled with a $134 billion cash cushion and early signs of profitability, suggests the Claude maker may be better equipped to turn the AI boom into sustainable profits.

D.A. Davidson Managing Director Gil Luria told CNBC on Tuesday that Anthropic’s S-1 weakens the view that the company is structurally unprofitable or financially unviable.

Luria said Anthropic has raised $141 billion and still holds about $134 billion, implying it has used roughly $7 billion of cash while building a business generating about $16 billion in quarterly revenue, or roughly $70 billion-$75 billion annualized.

He told CNBC that he expects third-quarter results to show GAAP and cash-flow profitability, although rising compute costs could keep profitability uneven in the near term.

Luria said second-quarter adjusted operating margin already reached 19% and expects adjusted profitability to continue.

He also cautioned that OpenAI and open-weight models are limiting Anthropic’s pricing power to the most advanced, mission-critical workloads.

Still, he pointed to nearly 12,000 customers spending more than $100,000 and about 1,900 spending more than $1 million as evidence of rapid customer expansion.

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Wellington Highlights Enterprise Pivot

Wellington Management Head of Late-Stage Growth Matt Witheiler, an Anthropic investor, said first-half revenue grew roughly 1,400% year over year, while compute costs increased about 300%.

Witheiler told CNBC on Monday that Anthropic’s shift toward enterprise customers proved critical to its growth. He highlighted roughly 12,000 customers spending more than $100,000, 1,300 spending above $1 million and 250 spending more than $10 million.

He sees Anthropic’s ability to remain at the frontier of model performance as its key competitive advantage.

Bessemer Sees Frontier Models Coexisting With Open Weight

Bessemer Venture Partners partner Byron Deeter said enterprises will continue using a mix of frontier, open-source, open-weight and older models depending on cost and performance needs.

He told CNBC on Monday that companies will still demand the strongest frontier capabilities for their most important workloads. Bessemer’s Anthropic stake is now the largest investment in the firm’s 116-year history by both cost basis and value.

Menlo Points to Rapid Product Cycles

Menlo Ventures partner Matt Murphy said Anthropic operates in a market where model improvement must happen continuously because customers can quickly shift toward better-performing alternatives.

Murphy told CNBC on Monday that 80% of Anthropic revenue comes from models released within the prior six months, underscoring the importance of rapid product development.

He said Anthropic has become Menlo’s largest investment and expects it to generate the biggest return in the firm’s history.

Cryptocurrency bettors currently see little risk of an imminent AI crash in the U.S., even as warning signs emerge from China.

Lessons From China?

Odds are shifting amid China’s brutal AI stock selloff that has erased hundreds of billions in market value. Market commentator Bull Theory declared that "the first AI bubble has burst,” adding that the U.S. is “flashing the same warning signs.”

A recent report, published by the Open Markets Institute and Americans for Financial Reform Education Fund, warned that AI-related spending is outpacing revenue from AI products and services, pushing companies to borrow more to finance their investments.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) also sounded the alarm, saying that soaring AI investments, growing corporate debt and inadequate regulatory oversight could expose the U.S. economy to a financial crisis reminiscent of the 2008 market crash.

Notably, Anthropic filed for an IPO at a valuation that is estimated to reach $2 trillion, despite losing $80.7 billion in the first half of the year.

news.author: Akanksha Bakshi
news.content:
NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) announced Tuesday an expanded artificial intelligence partnership focused on Meta’s Muse family of AI models. NVIDIA also plans to invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering.

NVIDIA and Meta Expand AI Model Collaboration

The companies aim to improve Muse model training and inference performance while reducing operating costs. The collaboration comes amid growing demand for AI agents capable of performing complex tasks.

Meta said its Muse models and AI agents, which run on NVIDIA infrastructure, have delivered strong benchmark results and attracted significant consumer downloads.

The companies are also exploring additional collaboration involving NVIDIA’s OpenShell Reference Architecture. This includes OpenShell for secure AI agent deployment and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring agent behavior.

Meta to Expand NVIDIA AI Infrastructure

As part of the partnership, Meta plans to expand its deployment of NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform and Vera CPUs. The infrastructure will support next-generation AI workloads while improving performance and energy efficiency.

Meta also intends to deploy NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4 technology to improve network efficiency and data throughput.

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said AI agents could reshape computing by enabling software to reason, use tools and complete tasks on behalf of users. He added that the partnership would focus on building efficient and secure AI infrastructure.

Meanwhile, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse remains central to the company’s efforts to develop personalized AI agents and advanced models for billions of users.

NVIDIA’s $3 Billion Investment Deepens Meta Ties

NVIDIA’s planned $3 billion equity investment further strengthens its long-standing relationship with Meta.

The expanded partnership highlights Meta’s continued spending on AI infrastructure and NVIDIA’s role in supplying the computing and networking technology needed to support advanced AI models.

Meta’s $95 Billion AI Funding Push Draws Analyst Support

The expanded partnership comes as Meta pursues plans to raise up to $95 billion to support its AI infrastructure expansion. The proposed financing includes $35 billion in underwritten equity offerings and a potential $60 billion at-the-market stock program.

BNP Paribas analyst Nick Jones expects Meta to maintain a rapid pace of AI product launches, supported by early adoption of Muse. Jones maintained an Outperform rating on Meta with a $940 price target.

Amkor Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:AMKR) stock traded higher Tuesday despite narrowly missing third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates and issuing guidance below Wall Street expectations.

The company reported earnings of 76 cents per share, missing the analyst consensus estimate of 78 cents.

Revenue totaled $1.99 billion, below the $2.01 billion consensus estimate.

Gross profit reached $364 million, while gross margin expanded to 18.3%, up 150 basis points sequentially and 400 basis points year over year.

The margin improvement reflected a stronger mix of advanced packaging services, partially offset by foreign exchange headwinds and a July earthquake at Amkor’s Kumamoto, Japan, facility.

The disruption reduced sequential gross margin by approximately 60 basis points, although the facility resumed full operations during the quarter.

Amkor held $2.4 billion in cash and short-term investments as of Sept. 30, 2026.

Business Performance and Fourth-Quarter Trends

Computing revenue rose 25% sequentially to a record high, while automotive and industrial revenue increased 7%. Both segments reached record revenue levels for the second consecutive quarter.

Management expects computing revenue to grow at a low-double-digit sequential rate in the fourth quarter, representing year-over-year growth of more than 50%. Automotive and industrial revenue is projected to increase at a low-single-digit sequential rate.

Communications revenue declined 8%, with management forecasting a high-single-digit sequential decline in the fourth quarter. Consumer revenue rose 10%, but the company expects a midteens sequential decline in the segment.

Component shortages are expected to continue weighing on premium smartphones and Internet of Things devices in the fourth quarter, with both the iOS and Android markets projected to decline sequentially.

Amkor continued expanding its high-density fan-out (HDFO) CPU programs, with an additional hyperscaler program ramping up in the third quarter. Two new 2.5D packaging programs for networking and data centers are expected to launch in the fourth quarter.

The company’s agreement with NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), involving its Songdo campus in South Korea, is also expected to support advanced packaging capacity.

Global Expansion and Capacity Investments

In Arizona, Amkor announced the second phase of its Advanced Packaging and Test Campus.

The two phases are expected to provide more than 90,000 square meters of cleanroom space and require a combined investment of approximately $12 billion.

The first phase remains on track for completion by the end of 2027, while construction on the second phase is expected to begin in late 2027.

In South Korea, construction began on two buildings at the Gwangju campus. The planned expansions are expected to increase Amkor’s footprint in the country by 40% compared with 2025 levels when completed in 2028.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Fourth-Quarter Outlook and Capital Spending

Amkor expects fourth-quarter earnings of 65 cents to 75 cents per share, below the analyst consensus estimate of 76 cents.

Revenue is projected at $1.9 billion to $2 billion, compared with the consensus estimate of $2.02 billion.

Management expects gross margin to expand sequentially by approximately 20 basis points, supported by a favorable product mix as computing revenue grows and system-in-package (SiP) revenue declines.

Continued foreign exchange headwinds are expected to partially offset the improvement.

The company narrowed its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to approximately $2.5 billion, primarily reflecting the timing of payments related to construction of the Arizona campus.

Capital spending is expected to increase in 2027 as Amkor invests in facilities in Arizona, South Korea and Vietnam. Customer advance payments are expected to help fund the investments.

Needham Analyst Cuts Price Forecast

Following the earnings release, Needham analyst Charles Shi maintained a Buy rating on Amkor but lowered his price forecast to $55 from $90.

Shi said Amkor’s 2.5D and HDFO programs remain on track, but smartphone and consumer demand has weakened further as a major customer reduced production amid component shortages.

Management remains optimistic about advanced packaging growth and expects higher capital spending in 2027 to expand data center CPU, XPU and networking capacity in Arizona and South Korea.

Customer prepayments are expected to help fund part of the investment, the analyst said.

Shi maintained his estimates for calendar years 2027 and 2028 but lowered his price forecast to reflect sectorwide compression in valuation multiples.

TradingView data going back to 1950 cover 19 midterm elections. In every case, the index was higher 12 months after the end of October in the election year.

The average gain was 16.6%, and the median was 16.3%. Even the weakest run, from October 2014 to October 2015, delivered about 3%. The strongest, after the 1954 vote, topped 33%.

The short-term picture is messier.

Read Also: The Average Stock Is Beating the S&P 500 by the Most Since April 2009: Is the Rotation Now Over?

From October to year-end, the S&P 500 rose in 13 of those 19 midterm years, with an average gain of 3.6%.

2018 shows the gap. The index slumped 7.6% in the last two months of that year, its worst post-midterm stretch in the sample.

Twelve months after the October close, however, it was up 12%.

Why Traders Start Watching This Week

Americans head to the polls on Election Day, Nov. 3, to elect all 435 House members and about a third of the Senate.

For a historical perspective, Dimitri Speck, founder and chief analyst at seasonal-research firm Seasonax, examined the narrower window around Election Day across 23 midterms since 1934.

From five trading days before the vote to two days after, the S&P 500 rose in 22 of 23 cases, with an average gain of 2.74%.

The only miss came in 1994.

Tuesday’s close is the fifth trading session before Nov. 3. In other words, the window opens today.

Speck links the move to pre-election optimism. He said the rise “is clearly triggered by these elections, as evidenced by the high accuracy rate.”

Bank of America Expects Strong Finish To 2026, But With a Caveat

Paul Ciana, technical strategist at Bank of America Global Research, sees midterm years as the soft spot of the four-year presidential cycle, at least until the fourth quarter.

Since 1940, the S&P 500 has averaged a 4.22% gain in midterm years, compared with 8.85% across all years, according to Ciana.

The fourth quarter flips that.

The index rose in 86% of midterm-year fourth quarters, by an average of 6.6%, against a 78% hit rate and a 3.87% average gain for all years.

Ciana summed up the S&P 500’s midterm profile as “an underdog, but Santa rally outperforms.”

He also flagged the exception that matters most for 2026, the second year of President Donald Trump‘s second term. In 2018, the second year of his first term, the S&P 500 ended the year down more than 6.5%, with no Santa rally.

Read Also: Tech-to-Defensive Rotation, GM Stock Logs Worst Week Since 2023: This Week on Wall Street

Not Everyone Wants to Buy Before the Vote

The S&P 500 — as tracked by the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:SPY) — closed Monday at 7,676.77, up 11.6% this year and about 2.1% below its record high of 7,844.52.

Ed Yardeni, president at Yardeni Research, is in no rush.

He kept a 7,900 year-end target for the S&P 500, about 3% above Monday’s close, and named an escalation of the Middle East war as their main concern.

He said they see some buying opportunities, but “better ones are likely after the November 3 midterm elections.”

The likely outcome also matters for what comes next.

Samuel Tombs, chief U.S. economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, expects divided government to freeze fiscal policy, with President Trump vetoing Democratic spending plans and new tariffs becoming less likely. In his view, less fiscal support should slow growth and give the Federal Reserve room to start easing next summer.

On Polymarket, traders give Democrats a 91.5% chance of winning the House and a 65.5% chance of taking the Senate, the latter up 1 percentage point over the past week.

History offers a tailwind, not a guarantee. Nineteen midterms is a small sample, and 2018 showed how quickly the fourth quarter can break the pattern even when the following year rewards patient investors.

Fundstrat Capital Chief Investment Officer Tom Lee is purchasing technology equities during the current market correction. He outlines six factors supporting his sustained belief in artificial intelligence (AI) investments despite recent fund underperformance.

Fund Performance Context

In his update for the week of Oct. 19, Lee, who serves as the lead portfolio manager for the Granny Shots ETF suite, acknowledged recent portfolio declines.

The Fundstrat Granny Shots US Large Cap ETF (NYSE:GRNY) fell 5.44% over the past week, from $28.45 on Oct. 9 to $26.90 on Oct. 23, bringing its year-to-date return to 9.69% compared to a 12.14% rise for the S&P 500, as of Monday’s close.

According to Lee, the bottom five performers in the GRNY portfolio were all AI bottleneck companies: Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC), Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU), Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE:VRT), KLA Corp. (NASDAQ:KLAC), and Arista Networks Inc. (NYSE:ANET). Despite these figures, Lee stated, “I’m buying this AI dip.”

Read Also: Tom Lee Predicts S&P 500 At 8,400 By Year-End, Says Midterm Elections Could Trigger ‘Risk-On’ Rally in Tech Stocks and Crypto: ‘We Are in an Unprecedented Time’

The Six Pillars of AI Conviction

Lee detailed his “six reasons why we have conviction about the AI trade” to address current investor concerns.

  • First, Lee described AI breakthroughs as “otherworldly,” noting OpenAI models recently solved 771 math problems in three hours, representing 81% of math discoveries over the past three years.
  • Second, Lee stated AI is beginning to “drive productivity,” citing an increase in S&P revenue per worker since ChatGPT’s launch.
  • Third, Lee argued that hardware supply constraints indicate the industry is not oversupplied.
  • Fourth, he framed substantial AI funding needs positively, stating that market nerves are raising capital costs, which is “preventing a bubble from forming.”
  • Fifth, Lee noted that heavy hedge fund shorting “looks like capitulation,” adding that he sees a general derisk ahead of the midterms.
  • Finally, he offered a historical analog, comparing the “correction we’re seeing today in the AI stocks” to Cisco in 1997. He noted Cisco Systems Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) fell 40% before mounting a 100-fold rally over the next two years.

Macroeconomic Tailwinds

Lee concluded by pointing to macroeconomic shifts, stating that the 10-year Treasury yield has sunk since the Jackson Hole symposium, which he labeled a “dovish development.”

He also noted that the odds of a December Federal Reserve rate hike dropped to 67%. Driven by these factors, Lee asserted that markets are a “coiled spring at the moment.”

How Has the Stock Market Performed?

The S&P 500 index has advanced 12.14% year-to-date. Similarly, the Nasdaq Composite index was up 14.97%, and the Dow Jones gained 9.94% YTD.

On Monday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) and Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ), which track the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, respectively, closed higher. Michael Burry says the stock market’s latest record high resembles the March 2000 dot-com bubble peak more than any other top in modern history.

In an Oct. 24 Substack post, Burry examined all 982 S&P 500 record closes since 1980. He scored each on seven measures of market internals, including the share of stocks near their highs and the share stuck in deep drawdowns.

  • PYPL stock is moving after earnings. Get all the details and data here. 

Two dates ranked at or beyond the 95th percentile of weakness on all seven: March 2000 and Oct. 6, 2026, the most recent record for the index tracked by the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (NYSE:SPY). No other record high in 46 years did. Burry says the pattern first appeared this year on May 27.

A Narrow Rally

Only 19.3% of S&P 500 members traded within 10% of their 10-year highs at the Oct. 6 record, a reading in the 99.5th percentile. Fewer than 100 stocks made up the leadership group, something seen only once before, in March 2000, when the Nasdaq-heavy names behind the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) went vertical.

Those leaders also look tired. Burry found 58% of them sat 5% to 10% below their peaks, the highest share on record. March 2000 came in second at 40%.

At the other end, 23% of index members are what Burry calls "Busted," down more than 40% from their highs. The group sits a median 55% below its peaks.

Read Also: Michael Burry Eyes the Exit on Walmart, Alphabet and Valero

Priced Like 2000

Using his adjusted earnings figures, Burry estimates the S&P 500 trades at about 32 times earnings. The 2000 market traded at roughly 32 to 34 times.

However, the two eras differ. The 10 largest companies traded at 50 times trailing earnings in 2000 against 33 times today. Busted stocks were far cheaper back then, however, with a median of 10.2 times earnings versus 17.2 times now.

See More: Top Value Stocks

The 2000 Playbook

After the 2000 top, leaders posted a median 33% decline over 12 months and 50% over 18 months. Busted stocks rose a median 19% and 18% over the same stretches.

Burry cautions the pattern does not always hold. After the October 2007 peak, every group fell more than 40% over 18 months. Deep discounts offered little protection heading into the 2020 COVID crash either.

Still, he is positioned for a repeat. Burry holds beaten-down names such as Lululemon Athletica Inc. (NASDAQ:LULU), PayPal Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL) and Adobe Inc. (NASDAQ:ADBE), set against short positions in AI and semiconductor stocks, a corner of the market tracked by funds like the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH).

Early returns lean his way. From Oct. 6 through Oct. 19, the 114 Busted stocks gained a median 3.2% while the S&P 500 fell 1.6%.

Burry called the move "almost certainly an indication of nothing."

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) short-term holders in profit have cooled to around 70% from nearly 100% in late September, a shift Glassnode calls a better entry point for buyers.

Why Glassnode Sees This as a Better Entry

Glassnode posted on X Tuesday that recent Bitcoin buyers have left the strong sell zone. In late September, almost all short-term holder supply sat in profit, a level that often signals heavy profit-taking risk. 

That figure has since cooled to about 70%, which Glassnode says makes this a considerably better entry than a month ago for anyone expecting the uptrend to resume.

Moreover, widely-followed market analyst Rand Group posted on X that every Bitcoin bottom on the chart was built by people capitulating and selling. 

The post framed the current pullback as a test of conviction and asked traders whether they would hold through it or provide the liquidity that fuels the next cycle.

Why Gillen Sees Both $60,000 and $100,000 as Possible

As Benzinga reported Tuesday, Milk Road analyst John Gillen said on the Milk Road Show that Bitcoin’s resilience near $80,000 suggests the recent rally remains intact despite macro uncertainty. 

He said both $60,000 and $100,000 remain realistic targets for Bitcoin before the end of the year.

Gillen said a pullback toward the 50-week moving average, between $76,000 and $78,000, would count as a normal retest rather than a failed rally. 

A convincing break below $75,500 could hand control back to the bears, while a drop toward $60,000 would raise more serious questions about the recovery. 

He pointed to more than $6 trillion sitting in money market funds as a potential source of liquidity that doesn’t require Fed intervention to push Bitcoin higher.

Why Ansem Turned Bearish on Bitcoin and Ethereum

Widely-followed trader Ansem posted on X that he’s bearish on Bitcoin, Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH) and large-cap stocks, arguing both tokens broke their mid-timeframe trend and could fall below $82,000 for Bitcoin and $2,400 for Ethereum. 

He pointed to the Nasdaq’s recent breakout failing to hold and Meta’s post-earnings selloff last week as signs that AI momentum stocks are forming a parabolic blowoff top.

Ansem said investors want clearer proof that heavy AI capital spending is actually translating into profit, and flagged this week’s FOMC meeting and a wave of earnings releases as catalysts for added volatility. 

He added that he isn’t bearish on the longer timeframe and expects a pullback before Bitcoin and Ethereum resume climbing.

Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) and Anthropic finalized $63 billion in hardware financing, prompting commentator Jim Cramer to state the transaction is excellent for all parties while noting reporters would scrutinize Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) over a comparable agreement.

The Deal and Cramer’s Reaction

Bank of America Corp. (NYSE: BAC), Blackstone Inc. (NYSE: BX), Citigroup Inc. (NYSE: C) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) committed $63 billion to finance Broadcom artificial intelligence chips for Anthropic. A newly formed special purpose vehicle will utilize the financing to purchase Broadcom’s XPU accelerators and lease them to Anthropic, with deliveries commencing in 2027.

Bank of America, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley are arranging the first-lien portion, while Blackstone is the sole provider of the second-lien financing. Broadcom is providing residual value support for the first-lien amount.

Reacting to the arrangement, Cramer posted on X, “I think this Broadcom deal is excellent for all involved but the press would never stop hectoring Nvidia if it did this deal.”

Read Also: Dan Ives Says Anthropic Could Be Worth $3 Trillion Eventually, Calls It ‘Hearts and Lungs’ of AI Trade

Hock Tan’s Leadership Highlighted

The Wall Street Journal reported that lenders considered abandoning the transaction, termed “Project North Star,” due to risk concerns and rising interest rates. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan held weekend discussions with bank executives, agreeing to higher interest rates and offering guarantees against losses if Anthropic defaults.

Cramer attributed the agreement’s viability directly to the CEO, stating, “Cramer said the Broadcom deal works because of Hock Tan. “It is why it is a high quality deal. There will not be others like it because there is only one Hock.”

How Has AVGO Performed?

The stock was lower by 7.05% over the last year, down 4.89% year-to-date, and lower by 6.70% over the last month. The stock is up 3.85% at $341.85 on Tuesday.
